rounds.text: The valuation of Hisar Metal Industries Ltd is severely disconnected from fundamental reality, as a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at just Rs 61 per share against a market price of Rs 153, representing a negative margin of safety of 150.6% [E44, E45]. Compounded annual performance metrics reveal structural deterioration, highlighted by a 3-year compounded sales growth of -2%, 3-year compounded profit growth of -32%, and a 5-year compounded profit growth of -9% [E16, E20, E19]. Profitability metrics are deeply underwhelming, with an ROE of 5.3% and ROCE of 8.0% falling well short of sector benchmarks [E13, E12, E9, E10]. Financial leverage presents an escalating hazard, with borrowings expanding to Rs 87 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 70 Cr a year prior, driving the debt-to-equity ratio to 1.34x where debt exceeds net worth and triggering a low interest coverage warning [E38, E39, E58]. Operating margins are persistently contracting, showing a multi-year downward trend over the last six years and falling to 4% in the March 2026 quarter from 8% in the year-ago period [E30, E31, E32]. Market sentiment aligns with these fundamental vulnerabilities, as the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, exhibits a lagging relative-strength rating of 24, and has suffered a 12-month price return of -24.4% alongside high annualised volatility of 59.4% [E49, E50, E51, E53]. Conceded: [E34, E35, E36, E37, E40, E71].
